query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A machine‐learning–augmented predictive model that incorporates first‐principles–computed vibrational density‐of‐states features along with atomic mass‐variance and bond‐length disorder descriptors will more accurately identify equimolar high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with low phonon thermal conductivity than current mass‐variance–only empirical models.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar, single‐phase (FCC or BCC) high‐entropy alloys composed of 4–6 transition‐metal elements, with random element distribution and minimal second‐phase precipitates.
generation.intervention: Application of the predictive model combining DFT‐derived phonon density‐of‐states features, atomic mass‐variance, and local bond‐length disorder descriptors into a supervised machine‐learning framework.
generation.conditions: Room temperature (300 K), bulk polycrystalline samples with average grain size >1 μm, negligible porosity (<1%).
generation.structural_mediator: Descriptors quantifying atomic mass variance, local bond‐length disorder distribution, and phonon density‐of‐states signatures from small‐cell DFT calculations.
generation.mechanism: By explicitly including vibrational fingerprints and bond‐length disorder metrics, the model captures the dominant phonon scattering mechanisms from atomic‐scale disorder, reducing systematic bias present in mass‐variance–only approaches.
generation.predicted_outcome: Average reduction of mean absolute prediction error of lattice thermal conductivity by 20–30% relative to the current mass‐variance empirical model, with correct top‐decile ranking of low‐κ candidates in at least 80% of cases.
generation.baseline: Current empirical mass‐variance–only models (e.g., Slack‐based extensions) yield ~40% mean absolute error in k_L predictions for equimolar 4–6 element HEAs.
generation.boundary: Applicable only to equimolar 4–6 element HEAs in single‐phase FCC or BCC structures at 300 K; may not hold for non‐equimolar compositions, >6 elements, multiphase microstructures, or highly anharmonic systems.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate (±10% in error‐reduction estimate) due to limited available training data in the HEA composition space.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a blind validation set of ten equimolar 4–6 element single‐phase HEAs. Measure their room‐temperature lattice thermal conductivity via time‐domain thermoreflectance (TDTR). Predict k_L using both the proposed ML‐augmented model and the baseline mass‐variance model.
measurements: Predicted k_L values from both models
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the proposed model does not achieve at least a 10% lower mean absolute error in predicted k_L compared to the baseline model across the validation set, the hypothesis is falsified.
